text:
sophie chen: Quick sync — vendor (OpenForge Labs) wants their new 13B open-weight listed in cloud marketplaces + offered as a HW bundle with our partner SI. Need clarity on licensing carveouts, redistribution rights, and announcement cadence. @ana legal @raj patel please advise :eyes:

raj patel: thanks. do we have the vendor's license text? are they CC-BY, MIT, dual-licensed, or custom?

maya lópez: they sent a custom permissive grant + an attribution addendum. will drop PDF here. in short: allow commercial use, must preserve model provenance, and disallow downstream relicensing of weights without permission.

maya lópez: tagging @oliver grant from marketplace — are we ok listing a model with a "no relicensing" clause?

oliver grant: marketplace: short answer — yes, but requires product copy + legal flag so cloud marketplaces accept it. we need a redistribution appendix that clarifies distribution artifact (weights vs. packaged inference endpoint).

ana legal: hey all — quick read. the vendor's addendum has two risky bits: 1) broadly-scoped "no redistribution" clause and 2) mandatory attribution language that must be embedded in product UIs. both are negotiable but would block standard marketplaces if left as-is.

ana legal: proposed edits (high level):
- carve out: allow distribution of hosted-inference endpoints and platform-integrated artifacts (bundles) but prohibit raw weight dumps to third parties without express consent.
- attribution: allow attribution in docs/marketing and a link in UI footer rather than forced modal text.

sophie chen: that sounds reasonable. can you draft the short appendix we can use with vendors as a template? aim for 1-2 paragraphs.

ana legal: drafting now. sending a redline in ~30m.

marketplace-bot: New doc uploaded: https://redwood-internal/share/openforge-13b-license-addendum-draft.pdf (access: partnerships+marketplace).

raj patel: re: HW bundle — SI partner requires ability to distribute a packaged container (optimized runtime + quantized model) to their customers under our reseller agreement. vendor's "no relicensing" forbids that unless we add a reseller/packaging exception.

ana legal: add a reseller exception: permit distribution of packaged runtime/container images for deployment to end customers when shipped by Redwood or authorized channel partners, provided the vendor is attributed and end users cannot extract raw weights from the package. also include a reciprocity clause for security updates.

oliver grant: technical note: we should require a reproducible mechanism in the package that prevents weight extraction (e.g., encrypted segments + runtime key). ops needs that defined before we approve marketplace SKU.

maya lópez: open question for engineering: how strong of a "prevent extraction" guarantee do we need vs an attestation + T&C?

oliver grant: we usually accept a combination: packaging + attestation + a license restriction discouraging extraction. full-proof cryptographic protections are expensive.

ana legal: will include language: "packaged distribution permitted where reasonable technical controls and contractual restrictions prevent unauthorized extraction of raw weights." keeps it flexible.

sophie chen: excellent. timeline: can legal provide the template + a short internal checklist for marketplace & SI (ops/eng) by EOD tomorrow? we'll need that to commit to announcement dates with partner.

ana legal: yes — template + checklist by EOD tomorrow.

raj patel: ops/eng to review checklist asap after doc lands. i'll coordinate with SI for technical acceptance criteria.

maya lópez: i'll prep vendor comms: explain why we need the reseller carveout and the minimal packaging controls. keep it high-level.

oliver grant: ping me when checklist is in — i'll map to marketplace SKU requirements and flags for cloud vendors (Azure/GCP/AWS differ slightly).

sophie chen: action items recap: 1) @ana legal draft addendum + checklist (EOD tomorrow) 2) @raj sync with SI on packaging acceptance 3) @oliver map marketplace flags once checklist is in 4) @maya send vendor message after draft reviewed.

sophie chen: thanks team :party_parrot:

marketplace-bot: Reminder: schedule RFC review in #partner-rfc channel once documents are finalized.
